study.title: Neural Biomarkers for Identifying Atopic Dermatitis and Assessing Acupuncture Treatment Response Using Resting-State fMRI
study.study_design: Randomized, participant- and assessor-blind, sham-controlled trial with neuroimaging component
study.randomization: AD participants randomly received real acupuncture (n=27) and sham acupuncture treatment (n=14)
study.population: 41 mild-moderate AD patients and 40 healthy controls

extraction_notes.note: Sensory/interoceptive responses (e.g., deqi, pain, tingling) were not assessed or reported. The paper uses resting-state fMRI and does not report any participant sensation questionnaires during or after acupuncture needling.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures are not reported in this paper. The paper refers readers to a protocol paper (Kim J et al., 2021) for full trial details, which may contain these measures.
Adverse events are not mentioned in the paper.
Specific acupoints used in real and sham acupuncture are not described in this paper. The paper refers readers to the protocol paper (Kim J et al., 2021) for details.

Sham acupuncture procedure details (device, penetration, location, manipulation, intended sensation) are not described in this paper. Only 'sham acupuncture treatment (n=14; see protocol paper for more details)' is stated.

The baseline SCORAD, EASI, VAS values reported in Table 1 are for the full AD group (n=41). Post-treatment values are split by real (n=27) and sham (n=14) groups. It is unclear whether the baseline column applies to all 41 AD participants or separately to the two subgroups.

The contrast results text on page 4 mentions 'left superior/middle frontal gyrus (0.81, 0.81, p < 0.001/0.80, 0.80, p < 0.01)' for the AD vs HC classification. This appears to represent two separate ROIs (superior and middle frontal gyrus) with separate accuracy/AUC and p-values. These have been extracted as separate entries (mr_AD_HC_SFG_left and mr_AD_HC_MFG_left).

In the treatment responder results, 'left superior medial/middle frontal gyrus (0.82, 0.80/0.81, 0.84)' appears to represent two separate ROIs. These have been extracted as separate entries (mr_resp_sup_med_mid_frontal_left_1 and mr_resp_sup_med_mid_frontal_left_2).

The figure caption (Figure 2) provides additional ROI-level accuracy values that partially differ from or supplement the text (e.g., 'left precentral gyrus (0.80, 0.80)', 'right temporal pole (0.77, 0.77)', 'left fusiform gyrus (0.74, 0.74)', 'right precuneus (0.71, 0.70)' for AD vs HC; 'right lingual-parahippocampal-fusiform gyrus (0.90, 0.89)' noted separately from 'left fusiform gyrus (0.90, 0.89)' for responders). Not all figure-caption values appear verbatim in the main text results section. Extraction focused on main text results; figure caption values noted here for reference.

Coordinate space is listed as MNI in the neuroimaging_methods field. This is inferred from Table 2 which labels coordinate columns as 'MNI Coordinates (X, Y, Z)'. The main text does not explicitly state MNI space for the neuroimaging analysis.

No whole-brain neuroimaging coordinate table is reported. The neural results are presented as ROI-level classification performance metrics (accuracy, AUC) per Power atlas ROI, not as spatial statistical maps with peak coordinates.

The number of time points used in the LSTM model is stated as n=115 in Figure 1 caption ('Blood oxygen level-dependent signals of each time point (n=115)'), while the acquisition had 150 volumes. Discrepancy not explained in the text—likely due to preprocessing volume removal.
Smoothing kernel size is not explicitly reported. Only 'spatial smoothing' is mentioned as part of the FSL preprocessing pipeline.

The statistical significance for the AD vs HC classification for the following ROIs is stated as 'significantly greater prediction accuracy than the chance level' without an explicit p-value threshold: temporal pole, PCC, precuneus, right SMA, and middle temporal gyrus. Explicit p-values are only given for SFG left (p < 0.001), MFG left (p < 0.01), DLPFC (p < 0.001), and superior medial frontal gyrus (p < 0.01).
PMID is not provided in the paper. DOI is provided as 10.2147/JAA.S454807.
